interactions.label: Which single clinical feature most reliably distinguishes inflammatory from mech

params.question: Which single clinical feature most reliably distinguishes inflammatory from mechanical joint disease?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Warmth is more common in inflammatory arthritis, but it can be subtle and varies with ambient temperature. Morning stiffness duration is the more discriminating feature.

Correct. Stiffness lasting one hour or more points to inflammatory arthritis; under thirty minutes suggests mechanical disease. The narration identifies this as the single most discriminating question in all of rheumatology.
Both inflammatory and mechanical pain may partially respond to analgesics. Treatment response is a supporting feature, not the primary discriminator between the two patterns.
Both inflammatory and mechanical disease can produce effusions, though the character differs — boggy and warm versus cool. Morning stiffness duration remains more discriminating.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key discriminator is morning stiffness duration: one hour or more signals inflammatory arthritis, under thirty minutes points to mechanical disease. This single question directs all subsequent investigation.
Well done. Morning stiffness duration is the single most discriminating question in rheumatology — one hour or more for inflammatory, under thirty minutes for mechanical.

interactions.label: A 40-year-old woman has painful right shoulder movement. Active abduction is pai

params.question: A 40-year-old woman has painful right shoulder movement. Active abduction is painful and limited, but passive abduction by the examiner achieves full range without pain. What does this pattern indicate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In articular disease such as synovitis, both active and passive movement are restricted because the inflamed joint itself limits motion. Full passive ROM here points away from a joint cause.

answers.text: Periarticular pathology such as tendinitis or bursitis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. When only active movement is painful but passive range of motion is preserved, the problem lies outside the joint — typically in a tendon, bursa, or enthesis. This articular-versus-periarticular distinction is critical for directing the workup.
Cervical radiculopathy can cause shoulder pain, but it typically follows a dermatomal distribution rather than showing a clear active-versus-passive discrepancy isolated to the shoulder joint.
Rheumatoid arthritis causes synovitis, which restricts both active and passive movement. Preserved passive ROM makes a periarticular cause — not articular inflammation — far more likely.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: both active and passive ROM restricted = articular (joint) cause. Only active movement painful with preserved passive ROM = periarticular cause (tendon, bursa). This distinction changes the entire workup.
Excellent. When only active movement is painful with preserved passive range, the pathology is periarticular — a tendon, bursa, or enthesis — not the joint itself.

interactions.label: A positive rheumatoid factor confirms the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis.

params.question: A positive rheumatoid factor confirms the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: A positive rheumatoid factor does NOT confirm RA. RF is also found in Sjögren syndrome, chronic hepatitis C, and about 5% of healthy elderly individuals. The second principle of autoimmune testing states that no test is read in isolation — always integrate results with the clinical picture. Anti-CCP (~95% specificity) is the more confirmatory test.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Rheumatoid factor is also positive in Sjögren syndrome, chronic hepatitis C, and approximately 5% of healthy elderly individuals. No autoimmune test is read in isolation. Anti-CCP antibody, with roughly 95% specificity, is far more confirmatory for RA.

interactions.label: A patient with acute gout asks you to start allopurinol immediately to prevent f

params.question: A patient with acute gout asks you to start allopurinol immediately to prevent future attacks. What is the correct treatment plan to communicate?

answers.text: Start allopurinol now along with colchicine for the acute flare

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Starting allopurinol during an acute flare mobilises urate crystals, which prolongs and worsens the attack. The acute flare must resolve completely before urate-lowering therapy begins.

answers.text: Treat the acute flare first; start allopurinol only after full resolution with prophylactic colchicine cover

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Allopurinol must never be started during an acute gout attack. Treat the flare with colchicine or NSAIDs, wait for full resolution, then begin allopurinol with prophylactic colchicine for 3–6 months, targeting serum uric acid below 6 mg/dL.

answers.text: Withhold allopurinol permanently and manage each flare individually with NSAIDs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Urate-lowering therapy with allopurinol prevents recurrent attacks and is indicated for patients with frequent flares or tophi. It should be started — but only after the acute episode has fully resolved.

answers.text: Start allopurinol immediately and discontinue colchicine to avoid drug interactions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prophylactic colchicine should continue for 3–6 months after starting allopurinol. This cover prevents the flares that urate mobilisation can trigger during the early months of urate-lowering therapy.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct gout treatment sequence is: treat the acute flare first (colchicine or NSAIDs), wait for full resolution, then start allopurinol with prophylactic colchicine for 3–6 months, targeting serum uric acid below 6 mg/dL.
Correct approach. Never start allopurinol during an acute gout attack — resolve the flare first, then begin urate-lowering therapy with colchicine prophylaxis for 3–6 months.

interactions.label: A rheumatoid arthritis patient in DAS28 remission reports she has stopped workin

params.question: A rheumatoid arthritis patient in DAS28 remission reports she has stopped working and withdrawn socially. Her HAQ-DI score has worsened by 0.3 points. Which statement best justifies the need to expand her current monitoring approach?

answers.text: DAS28 alone adequately tracks disease control; her functional decline is unrelated to rheumatoid arthritis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: DAS28 measures inflammation, not function or lived experience. Around 25% of patients in DAS28 remission still report significant disability and depression. Functional decline in RA is directly linked to participation restriction.

answers.text: The HAQ-DI change exceeds the minimal clinically important difference, confirming functional decline despite biological remission

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A HAQ-DI change of 0.22 or more is clinically meaningful — her 0.3-point worsening confirms real functional decline. Biological remission (low DAS28) does not equal patient remission. Quality of life measures such as HAQ-DI and PHQ-9 must accompany disease activity scores at every consultation.

answers.text: She should be referred to psychiatry since rheumatologic care cannot address participation restriction

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ICF framework shows that impairment → activity limitation → participation restriction is a continuum. Addressing all three levels is part of comprehensive rheumatologic care. PHQ-9 screening (≥10 = moderate depression) should be integrated into the same consultation, not separated out.

answers.text: The DAS28 must be recalculated using a different formula before any conclusions are drawn

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The issue is not the DAS28 formula but its scope. DAS28 accurately tracks inflammation; it simply does not capture functional and psychosocial outcomes. Patient-reported measures are the missing layer.

overallFeedback.feedback: Biological remission (low DAS28) does not guarantee patient remission. Around 25% of patients in DAS28 remission still report significant disability. The HAQ-DI (MCID ≥0.22) and PHQ-9 (≥10 = moderate depression) must accompany disease activity monitoring at every consultation.

Well reasoned. A HAQ-DI change ≥0.22 is clinically meaningful. Biological remission and patient remission are not the same — both disease activity and patient-reported outcomes need tracking at every visit.
